To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
UML profiles are useful for designing ICPs, but the existing real-time UML profile is not suitable for modeling ICPs.
1) UML profiles for real-time protocols are not mature enough to be used in the industry.

the most suitable profile for designing ICPs is the MARTE profile, which is a UML 2.4 profile that provides a set of extensions to the UML 2 metamodel to address real-time and embedded systems modeling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of UML and its real-time extensions in the development process of ICPs.

1) the analysis of the applicability and suitability of UML and its profiles to design ICPs; 2) the identification and analysis of ICPs design requirements, and; 3) the development of UML profiles for designing ICPs.

the following aspects: (1) to review the state-of-the-art of real-time communication protocols and to identify the most important requirements of these protocols; (2) to identify the most relevant real-time UML diagrams which can be used in the design and development of ICPs; (3) to identify the main features of the most relevant real time UML profiles and to discuss their applicability to the design of ICPs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single profile that can support the design, development and validation of all types of real-time ICPs.
UML profiles for real-time communication protocols have not yet reached a level where it can be used for modeling and validating industrial communication protocols.
UML with its real-time profiles is an appropriate formalism for the design and analysis of ICPs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UML with its real-time profiles, can support ICP design and analysis.
the most important profiles are: UML-Profile-4-Real-Time-Systems, UML-Profile-for-Embedded-Systems and the UML-Profile for Schedulability, Performance and Time (UML-SPT) profile.
UML is a good choice for modeling real-time ICPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UML real-time extensions can be used for modelling ICPs and that the real-time UML extensions can be used to model the non-functional aspects of ICPs.
the UML real-time extensions are well-suited for modeling ICPs.
the UML profiles can be used as a common modeling platform for the ICPs.
